title: Convoy TAKA-909, 19 September 1944
eyebrow: South of Honshu and east of Formosa · BANG's third war patrol

paras.text: BANG's attacks on convoy TAKA-909 east of Formosa, as typed on her attack sheets, with her depth log and the 4th Surface Escort Division's record of the day.

No. 2 Tosei Maru sunk. BANG claimed one AK sunk and another probably sunk. CD-30 and Taian Maru, with army aircraft, attacked her and claimed "one enemy submarine sunk"; BANG surfaced that night after about 80 depth charges.

Takao to Kagoshima (inferred). The 4th Surface Escort Division's war diary names the escorts and only the ship sunk; BANG saw 8 merchantmen including an AO, and 5 or more escorts. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:taka-909]].

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.
BANG kept zone K (−10) throughout. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Neither Japanese record for this patrol gives a time: combinedfleet.com's account of convoy No. 3905 and the 4th Surface Escort Division's daily summary for TAKA-909. Each is drawn at the time of the attack it matches, and marked so. FRUPAC's intercept has No. 3905's ships "torp & sunk 1520/09" (1520 I = 1620 K, between Attacks 1 and 2).

No Japanese record has been found yet for Attacks 5 and 6 (20–21 September); the 4th Escort diary has no attack on those days. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as BANG saw it.

BANG's third war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802831). The 4th Surface Escort Division / Okinawa Base Force war diary, September 1944, via JACAR (C08030144100, National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy No. 3905 from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.note: The record gives no time; drawn at the time of the attack it matches (Attack 3). 4th Surface Escort Division / Okinawa Base Force war diary, September 1944, 作戦経過概要 (daily operations summary), column 19. No time given. The "submarine sunk" was BANG, which surfaced that night after about 80 charges. 東勢 is read Tosei (DANFS: 507-ton tanker No. 2 Tosei Maru). TAKA = Takao to Kagoshima. The columns for the 20th and 21st have no attack, so nothing yet for BANG's Attacks 5-6 (2315 I on the 20th)

events.title: Ordered 400 ft
events.words: Went immediately to 400 feet as I had seen another escort ... at about 2000 yards with a 0° angle on the bow.

events.title: Ordered 450 ft (80)
events.words: Very deliberate depth charging began 4 minutes after firing. Three escorts ... let us have about 80 charges in patterns of 3 6 or 9 during the next 4½ hours. We were running silent at 450 feet under a 24 degree negative gradient.

paras.text: Attacked by BANG on 19 September 1944 off the north-east coast of Formosa. The Okinawa diary names six escorts and the one ship lost, No. 2 Tosei Maru, and says CD-30 and Taian Maru with army aircraft attacked the submarine and claimed it sunk. BANG surfaced that night after about 80 depth charges.

**Route, sailing and cargo: not recorded** in the records read. "Takao to Kagoshima" is inferred from the convoy code (タカ, the Takao–Kagoshima series) and the course; the 1st Surface Escort Division's September charts (jacar:C08030141500 pp. 45–55) have no chart for this route. BANG counted eight merchantmen, one an oiler.

No other US boat's attack on TAKA-909 has been found: the diary's columns for the 18th–21st have only this attack and, on the 20th, an attack on the depot ship Jingei far to the east (N27-12.5 E127-10.0; not BANG's).
To find: TAKA-909's sailing from Takao (the Takao Guard District's September 1944 diary) and its ships.
